h1: Best Platforms for Individual Course Creators vs Coaching Institutes (2026): What Each Needs and Which to Pick
dek: A solo educator and a coaching institute need different things from a platform. This guide sets out the difference, compares nine options with prices from each official site, and shows how to grow from one to the other without switching.
cover_alt: Solo educator or coaching institute: which platform fits, nine options compared with prices checked on 24 Oct 2026
audience: Solo educators and coaching institute owners in India choosing a course platform
intro: The best platform for an individual course creator is one that keeps fixed costs low and puts your own brand first; the best platform for a coaching institute is one that handles several teachers, batches and a shared brand. For a solo educator, Exly suits a coach selling from a checkout page, Graphy suits a creator with a large audience, and AllCoaching suits an educator who wants their own website and app. For an institute, Classplus offers a flat yearly price, Edmingle is built for training businesses with batches and branches, and AllCoaching adds separate teacher logins to the same academy, so a solo educator can grow into an institute without moving.
We are AllCoaching, so weigh that. Every competitor figure below comes from the company's own website, checked on 24 Oct 2026, and we say where another platform fits better than ours.

Throughout, "individual course creator" means a solo educator: one person teaching NEET biology, spoken English or yoga under their own name. "Institute" means a team of teachers running batches under one brand.
takeaways: Solo and institute needs differ in who teaches, what is sold, how students pay and what breaks first; pick for the one you are, and the one you will be in a year.
Solo picks: Exly (no upfront fee + 10%), Graphy (creators with an audience; rupee prices not confirmed), TagMango (community-led), AllCoaching (own website and app).

Institute picks: Classplus (₹29,999 a year listed), Edmingle (from ₹7,499 a month billed annually, branches and batches), AppX (done for you, price not listed), AllCoaching (teacher logins in your own academy).

AllCoaching fits both: 0% commission on Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month), or Starter at ₹6,999 a year plus 10% only when you sell, with your own domain, Android app (iOS app on Pro) and separate teacher logins; GST extra.
Udemy and Unacademy are places you teach on, not platforms you run; neither gives you your own brand, domain or app.
Signs you are becoming an institute: a second teacher, batches running in parallel, and parents asking for updates.

sections.h2: How we compared platforms for solo educators and institutes
sections.html:
We compared nine platforms educators in India shortlist: AllCoaching, Exly, Graphy, TagMango, Learnyst, Classplus, Edmingle, AppX and Teachmint, plus a note on Udemy and Unacademy. We used five checks.

  1. Who it says it is built for, in its own words.
  2. Published price and fee on sales, from its own pricing page.
  3. Own brand: own domain and own Android app (iOS app on Pro), and what they cost.
  4. Team features it publishes: teacher logins, batches, branches.
  5. How you start: free trial, no-upfront-fee plan or a demo.
Disclosure: AllCoaching publishes this guide. Competitor figures link to their official pages and carry the date we checked them (24 Oct 2026). Prices change; check the source before you decide. If you spot an error, write to contact@allcoaching.in and we will correct it.

sections.h2: Individual course creator vs coaching institute: what actually differs
sections.html:
A solo educator and an institute both sell teaching online, but they run different businesses. The table shows the differences that change which platform fits.

Solo educatorCoaching institute
Who teachesYouSeveral teachers, often with an owner who does not teach every class
What you sellCourses, test series, PDFs, sessionsBatches by class, subject and time slot, plus test series
How students payOne payment per courseOften a course fee for the year or term; ask each platform about instalments
Where students come fromYouTube, Instagram, WhatsApp, searchWalk-ins, parents, referrals, plus the same online channels
What breaks firstAdmin time: payments, access and links by handCoordination: who teaches which batch, logins, records

That matters because many institutes in India began as one teacher with a YouTube channel and grew. What one platform cannot do well is be built only for schools or only for one-person creators and stretch to the other.}} {{fig:before-after|Before and after for a growing institute: teachers sharing one login, a WhatsApp group per batch, fees in Excel, recordings on Drive and tests on Google Forms, compared with one academy with separate teacher logins, website, Android app (iOS app on Pro), live classes and UPI checkout|The mess grows with every teacher you add. One academy keeps it in one place.}}

sections.h2: What an individual course creator needs from a platform
sections.html:
A solo educator needs a platform that costs little before students pay, looks like their own brand, and takes admin off their hands. In order of what usually matters most:

  1. Low fixed cost. A trial or small yearly plan, so you are not paying for a year before your first batch sells.
  2. Your own brand. A website on your own domain and, as students grow, your own app, so students remember you and not the platform. See building a personal brand as an educator.
  3. UPI checkout that gives access automatically. No more checking screenshots and sending links by hand.
  4. Simple setup from a phone or laptop. You are the teacher, editor and support desk.
  5. Live classes and tests in the same place as recorded lessons.
  6. A way to leave. Student and payment data you can export.

sections.h2: What a coaching institute needs from a platform
sections.html:
An institute needs everything a solo educator needs, plus control over a team: who teaches which batch, who can see what, and one brand across all of it.

  1. Separate teacher logins. Shared passwords are the first thing to break. Each teacher should manage their own batches.
  2. Batches. Students grouped by class, subject and time slot, with the right content and live classes for each.
  3. One brand for the institute. Website, app and checkout under the institute name, not each teacher's.
  4. Fees the way you collect them. If you take fees in instalments, ask each platform how it handles them before you sign up.
  5. Records the owner can see. Students, payments and test results in one place.
  6. Branches, if you have them. Edmingle publishes branch management; for others, ask.

Our guide to a multi-teacher coaching platform goes deeper into running a team online.

sections.h2: 9 platforms compared: which fits solo, institute or both
sections.html:
Each platform below is described the way its own company describes it, with the published price and whether it fits a solo educator, an institute, or both.

Our platform · disclosure

1. AllCoaching · fits both

Good at
An academy you build yourself, like Shopify for coaching: website on your own domain, your own Android app (iOS app on Pro), courses, tests, PDF notes, unlimited live classes and UPI checkout. Institutes add separate teacher logins and batch ownership in the same studio.
Published price
Growth ₹7,999/month and Pro ₹14,999/month at 0% commission (keep 100%), or ₹79,990 and ₹1,49,990 paid yearly; Starter ₹6,999/yr + 10% on sales; GST extra; 7-day free trial, no card.[1]
Check
Teacher pay inside an institute is yours to handle; the platform does not split revenue between teachers. Ask about anything specific you need, such as fee instalments.
Best for
A solo educator who expects to add teachers later, and small to mid-size institutes that want their own brand.

2. Exly · fits solo

Good at
Storefront, payments, CRM and WhatsApp and email automation for coaches selling courses, consultations and digital products.
Published price
Starter: no upfront fee + 10% commission; Pro ₹30,000/yr + 6%; Premium ₹1,08,000/yr + 3%. Org members are ₹1,000 per user a year; a mobile app is an add-on from ₹60,000 a year.[2]
Check
GST treatment is not stated.
Best for
A solo coach selling sessions, cohorts or digital products.

3. Graphy · fits solo

Good at
An all-in-one platform for creators: website builder, branded mobile apps, digital products and AI sales agents.
Published price
Graphy publishes plans on graphy.com/pricing, but prices are shown by country and we could not confirm the Indian rupee plans on 24 Oct 2026; check the page from India. 7-day free trial.[3]
Check
The rupee price, the fee per sale and which plan includes the iOS app. Spayee's website now redirects to Graphy.
Best for
A solo educator with a large YouTube or Instagram audience.

4. TagMango · fits solo

Good at
Courses, community and automation for coaches, with an AI add-on stack and optional branded apps.
Published price
Basic: no fixed fee + 10% (up to 200 students); Pro ₹5,000/month + 5.5%; Advanced ₹15,000/month + 3.5%; Ultimate ₹30,000/month with zero commission; all + GST.[4]
Check
Custom domain via a ₹24,999 + GST yearly setup; branded apps ₹74,999 + GST setup.
Best for
Community-led coaching programmes run by one coach.

5. Learnyst · fits both, test-heavy

Good at
Courses, mock tests and live classes with content protection and test series.
Published price
Launcher ₹10,000/yr + 10%; Professional ₹8,999/month (₹8,099 billed annually), Premium ₹14,999/month, Business ₹49,999/month, all with 0% transaction fees; taxes extra.[5]
Check
Branded apps start from Premium and are published under Learnyst's developer account.
Best for
Exam educators and academies whose main product is a test series.

6. Classplus · fits institutes

Good at
A branded teaching app plus website for coaching businesses, with an admin portal, unlimited recorded courses, live classes and enrolments listed.
Published price
₹29,999 for 1 year or ₹39,999 for 2 years.[6]
Check
GST, any fee on sales, renewal price and an iOS app are not stated on the pricing page.
Best for
Coaching institutes that want one flat yearly price.

7. Edmingle · fits institutes

Good at
An "AI-powered LMS purpose-built for professional training and skilling businesses", with multi-cohort batches, branch management and white-labelled academies.
Published price
Core ₹7,499/month, Prime ₹14,999/month, Power ₹29,999/month, billed annually; taxes extra; 7-day free start.[7]
Check
A fee on sales is not stated; branded Android from Prime and branded iOS from Power.
Best for
Training businesses and larger institutes with several batches or branches.

8. AppX · fits institutes

Good at
Branded website and apps (Android, iOS, desktop) set up for you; it says "Launch your own branded app and website for your courses and community. No code needed."
Published price
Not listed on its website (checked 24 Oct 2026); it starts with a free personalised demo.[8]
Check
The yearly cost, any fee on sales and who can change the app after launch.
Best for
Institute owners who prefer a done-for-you setup.

9. Teachmint · fits schools

Good at
Classroom technology; its website now leads with Teachmint X, an "AI-Powered Connected Classroom Device" for schools, higher education and coaching.
Published price
Not listed on its website (checked 24 Oct 2026); you book a demo.[9]
Check
Whether the offer is built for selling courses online or for running classrooms.
Best for
Schools and offline institutes that want smart-classroom hardware.

What about Udemy and Unacademy? They are places you teach on, not platforms you run. Udemy is a global course marketplace with its own learner base; its instructor revenue-share page could not be retrieved on 24 Oct 2026, so we do not quote a figure.[10] Unacademy describes itself as "India's largest online learning platform"; we found no public educator programme page.[11] Either can sit next to your own academy, but neither gives you your own brand, domain or app.

sections.h2: What a solo educator and an institute pay as sales grow
sections.html:
Solo platforms tend to charge little upfront and take a share of sales; institute platforms tend to charge a larger flat price. The chart adds each published price to its published fee at five sales levels.

{{fig:cost|Total yearly cost at sales up to ₹10 lakh from published prices for AllCoaching, Exly, Classplus and Edmingle|Before GST. Exly's line leaves out its app add-on; Classplus and Edmingle lines are listed prices only, because their pages do not state a fee on sales.}} {{cost_table}}

The honest reading: for a solo educator selling up to about ₹8 lakh a year, Exly Starter costs less than AllCoaching on published prices if you do not need your own app; with Exly's app add-on from ₹60,000 a year, AllCoaching costs less at every level. For an institute selling above about ₹2.3 lakh a year, Classplus's flat listed price is lower on paper than AllCoaching, before any fees Classplus may charge. Edmingle Core, at ₹89,988 a year billed annually, costs more than AllCoaching at every sales level we checked, since AllCoaching Growth is ₹79,990 paid yearly at 0% commission, and it includes branch features a large training business may need.

sections.h2: Which platform fits your kind of educator business
sections.html:
Solo educator, just starting

Keep the cost before your first sale small and test demand. Our guide to the lowest-risk LMS for early-stage educators compares free trials.

Solo educator with a following on YouTube or Instagram

You already have demand; your own website and app turn followers into students who remember your name. See how to earn from a YouTube teaching channel with your own app.

Small institute with two to five teachers

Separate teacher logins and batches are the first must-haves. Compare totals at your real sales level rather than the headline price.

Large institute or chain with branches

Branch management and detailed operations may matter more than price. Edmingle publishes branch features; ask every vendor to show them in a demo or trial.

Not sure which you are

Choose a platform that serves both, so growing does not mean moving. Our ranked review of course selling apps in India compares ten options by use case.

sections.h2: How to grow from solo educator to institute without switching platforms
sections.html:
The smoothest path is to start on a platform that already supports teachers and batches, so that growing is a setting, not a move.

{{fig:switch|Four steps from solo educator to institute: build your academy, add your first teacher, organise batches, put the institute brand on everything|Growing should feel like adding a room, not moving house.}} {{steps}}

If you do need to change platforms on the way, follow our checklist on how to switch coaching apps without losing students.

items: Build your academy as a solo educator
Start the 7-day trial, connect your domain and upload one complete course with a demo lesson.
Add your first teacher with their own login
Give the new teacher a separate login and their own batch, instead of sharing your password.
Group students by class, subject or time slot so each batch sees the right lessons, tests and live classes.
Put the institute brand on everything
Use one name, logo and domain for the website and the Android and iOS app, so students see one institute.
Check students, payments and test results in one place, and export them when you need a copy.

faq: What is the best platform for individual course creators in India in 2026?

It depends on what you sell. Exly suits a coach selling from a checkout page with no upfront fee, Graphy suits a creator with a large audience, and AllCoaching suits a solo educator who wants their own website and Android app (iOS app on Pro), with 0% commission on Growth (₹7,999 a month) and Pro (₹14,999 a month), or Starter at ₹6,999 a year plus 10% of sales.
What is the best platform for coaching institutes in India in 2026?

Classplus suits institutes that want one flat yearly price (₹29,999 listed), Edmingle suits training businesses with batches and branches, AppX suits owners who want a done-for-you setup, and AllCoaching suits institutes that want their own brand with separate teacher logins.
What is the difference between an individual course creator and a coaching institute?

A solo educator teaches and sells their own courses; an institute runs several teachers and batches under one brand. That changes what matters most: low fixed cost and personal brand for a solo educator, teacher logins and batch control for an institute.
Can the same platform serve both solo educators and institutes?
Yes, if it lets you start alone and add teachers and batches later without moving students. AllCoaching includes separate teacher logins and batch ownership on every plan.
When should a solo educator move to an institute setup?
When a second teacher joins, when batches run at the same time, or when parents and students need updates you cannot send by hand. Those are signs you need teacher logins and batches.
Are Udemy and Unacademy platforms for individual course creators?
They are places you teach on rather than platforms you run. Neither gives you your own brand, domain or app, and Udemy's revenue share could not be verified on its own page on 24 Oct 2026.
What should a coaching institute check before choosing a platform?
Separate teacher logins, batches, how fees and instalments are handled, who owns the app listing, the full yearly cost at your sales level, and whether you can export your data.
